info.title: WordPress REST API (Supernala selection)
info.description: A reviewed subset of the WordPress core REST API (wp/v2) on the Owner's own site, signed in with a username and an application password over HTTPS. Paths, parameters and bodies follow https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/reference/.

servers.description: The Owner's WordPress site, entered at setup.

get.description: Returns the user this connection signs in as: ID, name, and with `context=edit` their roles and capabilities. Use it to learn what the Bot may do on this site.

schema.description: `edit` returns raw (unrendered) title and content and needs edit rights; `view` is the public form.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

get.description: Returns the site title, tagline, time zone, date format, default category and posts per page. Needs an Administrator; other roles get 403, which is expected.

schema.description: Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

get.description: Searches published posts, pages and terms by words and returns each match's ID, title, URL, type and subtype. Use the ID with the matching get tool for details.

schema.description: Narrow by subtype, such as `post`, `page`, `category` or `post_tag`.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

get.description: Lists posts, newest first by default. Without `status` only published posts are returned; pass `status` (for example `draft`) to see others. Use `_fields` such as `id,title,status,date,link` to keep the list small.

schema.description: Statuses to include. Drafts, pending, scheduled (`future`) and private items need edit rights.
Only items published after this ISO 8601 date.
Only items published before this ISO 8601 date.
Only items by these user IDs.
Only the item with this slug.
Only posts in these category IDs.
Only posts with these tag IDs.
`edit` returns raw (unrendered) title and content and needs edit rights; `view` is the public form.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

post.description: Creates a post. It is a draft unless `status` says otherwise; create as `draft` and show the Owner the link before publishing. Returns the new post with its ID and link.

title.description: The post title, as plain text.

content.description:
The post body as HTML or WordPress block markup, such as `

Text

`.

excerpt.description: Short summary shown in lists and feeds.

status.description: `draft` keeps it private to editors; `publish` makes it public now; `future` schedules it for `date`; `pending` asks an editor to review; `private` is visible to logged-in editors only.

date.description: Publish date in the site's time zone, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`. Needed with status `future`.

author.description: User ID of the author; defaults to the connected user.

featured_media.description: Media ID of the featured image, from the media library; 0 removes it.

password.description: Protects the item with this password; empty string removes it.

categories.description: Category IDs; replaces the current list.

tags.description: Tag IDs; replaces the current list.

sticky.description: Pin the post to the top of the blog.

format.description: Post format, where the theme supports it.

get.description: Returns one post by ID. Use `context=edit` to get the raw title and content for editing, including drafts.

schema.description: `edit` returns raw (unrendered) title and content and needs edit rights; `view` is the public form.

delete.description: Moves one post to the trash. WordPress keeps trashed items for 30 days by default and an editor can restore them; nothing is deleted permanently.

get.description: Lists post categories with their IDs, names, slugs, parents and post counts. Use the IDs in `categories` when creating or updating posts.

schema.description: Only children of this category ID; 0 for top level.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

post.description: Creates a post category. Check `list_categories` first so you do not add a duplicate; WordPress refuses a name that already exists at the same level.

slug.description: URL slug; derived from the name when omitted.

parent.description: Parent category ID; 0 for top level.

get.description: Lists post tags with their IDs, names, slugs and post counts. Use the IDs in `tags` when creating or updating posts.

schema.description: Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

post.description: Creates a post tag. Check `list_tags` first; WordPress refuses a tag name that already exists.

slug.description: URL slug; derived from the name when omitted.

get.description: Lists comments, newest first. Without `status` only approved comments are returned; `hold` lists comments awaiting moderation and needs moderation rights.

schema.description: Only comments on these post or page IDs.
`edit` returns raw (unrendered) title and content and needs edit rights; `view` is the public form.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

post.description: Posts a comment as the connected user on a post or page, or a reply when `parent` is a comment ID. It is public at once when the user may moderate.

parent.description: Comment ID to reply to; 0 for a top-level comment.

post.description: Approves, holds or marks one comment as spam, or edits its text. Needs moderation rights.

status.description: `approved` shows it, `hold` hides it pending review, `spam` marks it as spam.

delete.summary: Move a comment to the trash
delete.description: Moves one comment to the trash, where a moderator can restore it. Nothing is deleted permanently.

get.description: Lists items in the media library with their IDs, titles, alt text, type and URLs. Use an image's ID as `featured_media`, or its URL in content. Uploading new files is not available here.

schema.description: Only media attached to these post or page IDs.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

get.description: Returns one media item by ID with its URLs, sizes, alt text and caption.

schema.description: `edit` returns raw (unrendered) title and content and needs edit rights; `view` is the public form.
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.

post.description: Changes a media item's title, alt text, caption or description. The file itself is not changed.

alt_text.description: Alternative text read by screen readers; describe the image.

description.description: Longer description on the attachment page.

get.description: Lists users who have published content, with their IDs and names, to choose an `author`. Listing everyone, with roles, needs an Administrator.

schema.description: Only users with these roles (Administrator only).
Comma-separated fields to return, such as `id,title,status,link`. Keeps responses small; content and rendered HTML can be large.
